items.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: So one time at the very beginning of Isaiah’s time with us I turned around and said, “Let’s do ‘Body and Soul’ in five.” And Isaiah turned to Mike and said, “Wow, that’s sort of cool.”

ctx.x: Well that’s a good place to start. I had the pleasure with about 200 plus other people of having you to Hamilton a couple of weeks ago and it was a marvelous concert. There was a couple of things I wanted to ask you about it. You have a terrific piano player with Isaiah Thompson, and there was a few moments throughout the night, he was sitting to your left, and you would lean over while you were playing and say something to him. And the person that was sitting next to me and I were sort of wondering, well what…

Well during the song it might be to — I might say like sometimes I say, “Here we go” and it means we’re finishing the song. Like we’ll be playing a tag [scats] “Here we go” [scats] and everybody knows. Sometimes I just say stupid things to him to make him laugh. So like between songs. Or I’ll just say we’re going to do this next and, you know and I’ll say like, “I almost did okay on that one” you know or something. Like trying to keep it a little lighter. But during the song sometimes I’ll yell out a new key, and…

same thing, I think Tadataka said the same thing, he says, “You only say ‘five’ for D flat.” He goes, “It’s like one of those weird things.” Because we trade fours I’ll say “fours.” But “five” is D flat. It’s one of those little communication things. When I was with Bucky it was always eyebrows were the communicator. So when you’re playing, if you’re playing this way and you look over and you saw him go like that it meant he was going to look at you, or in that case me, and I knew something — here there’s a…
